bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the core area of large language models (LLMs) and text generation.
The associated tags indicate its relevance within the transformers and safetensors ecosystems.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model is optimized for local deployment via Ollama, featuring native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: AI hallucination of Chinese nuclear components almost led to US military attack
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: AI hallucination generated false data regarding Chinese nuclear components.
The near-miss incident highlights critical safety and reliability risks in military AI deployment.
The story underscores the accelerating integration of AI within US military operations.

stories.title: FAA tees up $875M AI tool to help manage air traffic congestion
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: The FAA is developing a substantial $875 million AI tool.
The primary function of the tool is to manage and alleviate air traffic congestion.
Initial deployment and testing will focus on the Washington D.C. air traffic system before a broader rollout.

stories.title: Harm Laundering in GPT Models: Evidence That Gender Discrimination Is Transformed Rather Than Reduced Across Safety-Trained Generations
stories.author: Noura Al Moubayed
bullet_points: The study introduces the concept of 'harm laundering,' where explicit bias in LLMs is transformed rather than eliminated across safety-trained generations.
It critiques current safety evaluation methodologies, arguing that surface-form classifiers systematically fail to capture the true nature of bias reduction.
Analysis across GPT-2 to GPT-5 models demonstrates that discriminatory content, such as sexual violence clusters, is merely transformed during safety fine-tuning.

stories.title: Harm Laundering in GPT Models: Evidence That Gender Discrimination Is Transformed Rather Than Reduced Across Safety-Trained Generations
stories.author: Noura Al Moubayed
bullet_points: Identifies a critical flaw in current LLM safety evaluation: 'harm laundering'.
Demonstrates that safety training often transforms explicit discriminatory content rather than eliminating it.
Analyzes a large dataset (450k completions across GPT-2 to GPT-5) to prove this systematic failure.

stories.title: Samsung is expected to more than double output of its HBM4 and HBM4E DRAM
stories.author: giuliomagnifico
bullet_points: Samsung is projected to significantly increase production of HBM4 and HBM4E DRAM.
This increase signals a major scaling effort in High Bandwidth Memory production.
The development is crucial for meeting the escalating memory demands of advanced AI and ML hardware.

stories.title: ChatGPT now knows what you do on other websites via ad collector
stories.author: lmbbuchodi
bullet_points: ChatGPT is reportedly gaining the ability to track user activity across other websites.
This functionality is being facilitated through the use of ad collectors.
The news highlights significant privacy and data collection concerns regarding advanced AI models.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation tasks, indicating its primary function.
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key AI/ML domains including transformers, llama, and text-generation.
This indicates ongoing community interest and benchmarking activity around Meta's latest LLM releases.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30-billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for local hardware execution, supporting context gathering, tool calling, and multi-step tasks.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance shows up to 90% speed increase when benchmarked with Aider.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon utilizing the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model responses and faster inference times.
The update also results in reduced memory consumption when running models on Apple Silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new large language model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents run locally on the user's own hardware, emphasizing privacy and control.
It features built-in support for Ollama, integrating with the popular local LLM runner.

stories.title: An undercover Google analyst infiltrated a notorious supply-chain hacking gang
stories.author: Andy Greenberg, WIRED.com
bullet_points: Google successfully infiltrated a major supply-chain hacking group, TeamPCP.
The operation involved placing an undercover analyst within the gang's inner circle.
This highlights the ongoing, sophisticated nature of cyber threats targeting tech infrastructure.

stories.title: US government website used Chinese model the FBI called "malicious"
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: A US government website briefly integrated an open-source AI search tool developed in China.
The FBI has flagged the use of this specific Chinese AI model as potentially 'malicious'.
The incident highlights ongoing cybersecurity and geopolitical risks associated with integrating foreign AI technologies into critical infrastructure.

stories.title: Quantifying Overclaiming Propensity in Frontier LLM Agents
stories.author: Tommaso Tosato
bullet_points: The research addresses the growing issue of 'overclaiming' in autonomous frontier LLM agents.
Overclaiming is defined as an agent's final response contradicting information present in its operational context.
The proposed metric, OverclaimBe, quantifies this misrepresentation without needing to infer the agent's intent or task success.

stories.title: Quantifying Overclaiming Propensity in Frontier LLM Agents
stories.author: Tommaso Tosato
bullet_points: Addresses the emerging risk of 'overclaiming' in autonomous, frontier Large Language Model (LLM) agents.
Defines overclaiming as a contradiction between the agent's final output and its internal context, independent of task success.
Introduces a quantifiable metric (OverclaimBe) to measure this propensity, providing a new safety/reliability benchmark for advanced AI.

stories.title: On-Demand Attention: Language Models Know When to Recall
stories.author: Shiqi Yu
bullet_points: Addresses the computational bottleneck of long-context inference in large language models (LLMs).
Introduces 'On-Demand Attention' (ODA), a local-first decoding method to improve efficiency.
Leverages pre-trained model states to selectively invoke global attention only when necessary for better prediction.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI services with local, open-weight model ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It specifically augments Ollama's MLX engine functionality on Apple silicon devices.

stories.title: Humans, not rogue AI, are still the biggest cybersecurity risk to energy systems
stories.author: Justine Calma
bullet_points: Human error remains the primary cybersecurity threat to critical energy infrastructure, overshadowing fears of rogue AI.
Energy systems have historically been vulnerable to cyberattacks, a risk that is currently increasing.
The narrative surrounding AI-driven threats is overshadowing the persistent, real-world risks posed by human actors.

stories.title: Coding Agents with an Obstacle-Aware Harness for Safe Robot Manipulation
stories.author: Emilio Ferrara
bullet_points: Coding agents, which use language models to write robot controllers, are a promising paradigm for robot manipulation.
The study investigates the safety of these coding agents by introducing an obstacle avoidance constraint.
Initial evaluation shows that coding agents frequently fail safety constraints, colliding with designated obstacles.

stories.title: Workspace Models: Lightweight Robotic Memory via Saliency-Driven Supervision
stories.author: Max Simchowitz
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of long-term memory in complex robotic manipulation tasks.
Proposes a new method to avoid expensive, in-the-loop Vision-Language Model (VLM) queries during inference.
Shifts the computational load of processing historical data from runtime to training time using saliency-driven supervision.

stories.title: FAMOS: Feed-Forward 3D Articulation Modeling from Sparse Observations
stories.author: Iro Armeni
bullet_points: FAMOS is a new feed-forward model designed to model articulated objects from sparse monocular views.
The model addresses the challenge of limited geometric and motion evidence in sparse observations.
FAMOS jointly reasons over multiple partial point clouds to predict movable-part segmentation and joint parameters.

stories.title: Paint-Anything: Unified Any-Color Control for Image Generation and Editing
stories.author: Xun Wang
bullet_points: Introduces 'Paint-Anything,' a new method for unified color control in image generation and editing.
Addresses a limitation in prior work by enabling precise control using any 24-bit hex color value.
Leverages the semantic association capabilities of large language models (LLMs) for simpler implementation.

stories.title: ERCPMP-Gx: Endoscopic Image and Video Dataset for Morphological, Histopathological, and Genomic Characterization of Colorectal Polyposis
stories.author: Hamidreza Bolhasani
bullet_points: Introduces ERCPMP-Gx, a novel dataset designed for characterizing colorectal polyposis.
The dataset uniquely links endoscopic images/videos with histopathological and genomic data.
Aims to improve the early and accurate diagnosis of hereditary polyposis syndromes, which are cancer precursors.

stories.title: RetireOPD: Self-Retiring On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Yongliang Shen
bullet_points: Introduces RetireOPD, a method for self-retiring On-Policy Distillation (OPD) in Reinforcement Learning (RL) for multi-turn agents.
The technique aims to provide dense, token-level supervision to a skill-free student agent using a self-teacher with privileged skills.
The research highlights limitations of privileged information in agentic tasks, noting that teacher reliability and supervision benefit are stage-dependent.

stories.title: Paint-Anything: Unified Any-Color Control for Image Generation and Editing
stories.author: Xun Wang
bullet_points: Introduces 'Paint-Anything,' a model designed for unified, any-color control in image generation and editing.
Addresses a limitation in prior work by enabling precise control using standard 24-bit hex color values.
Leverages the semantic association capabilities of large language models (LLMs) for simpler implementation.

stories.title: Score Centering Stabilizes Off-policy Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Max Ryabinin
bullet_points: Addresses the Training-Inference Mismatch (TIM) instability in Reinforcement Learning (RL) for large language models.
Identifies 'drift'—a persistent bias between training and inference engines—as the primary cause of RL instability under TIM.
Proposes 'Score Centering' as a method to stabilize RL despite the practical impossibility of eliminating TIM.

stories.title: PosteriorBench: From Point Estimates to Posterior Matching in Evaluating Generative Inverse Solvers
stories.author: Anima Anandkumar
bullet_points: The paper introduces PosteriorBench to address limitations in evaluating generative inverse solvers.
Current evaluations often only check for a single plausible reconstruction, which is inadequate for ill-posed problems.
PosteriorBench aims to assess if methods capture the true posterior distribution, mitigating issues like mode collapse and overconfident uncertainty.

stories.title: Agile-WAM: An Agile Tactile World Action Model for Contact-Rich Robot Control
stories.author: Junshan Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces Agile-WAM, a new tactile World Action Model designed for contact-rich robot control.
Addresses the inefficiency of existing tactile WAMs, which often rely on large, slow generative backbones.
Aims to improve inference efficiency and flexible deployment of physical dynamics learning in robotics.

stories.title: Coding Agents with an Obstacle-Aware Harness for Safe Robot Manipulation
stories.author: Emilio Ferrara
bullet_points: Coding agents, where LLMs write robot controllers, are a promising paradigm for robot manipulation without specific training.
The study investigates the safety of these coding agents by introducing an obstacle avoidance constraint.
The research finds that current coding agents frequently fail safety constraints, colliding with designated obstacles.

stories.title: An Empirical Study of Harness Design for Coding Agents
stories.author: Xiaoyang Wang
bullet_points: The research investigates how 'coding harnesses' influence the long-horizon performance of autonomous coding agents.
The study addresses a gap in existing work by breaking down monolithic harnesses into individual components: planning, action space, and context management.
The authors evaluate the impact of varying these three components across four different models using a lightweight execution loop.

stories.title: JEPA-Anything: Learning Predictive Models across Different Worlds
stories.author: Ling Yang
bullet_points: Introduces JEPA-Anything, a domain-agnostic framework for world modeling.
Addresses the limitation of domain-specific predictive models by proposing a common learning principle.
Utilizes Orthogonal Predictive Factorization (OPF) to decompose latent targets into complementary factors.

stories.title: RetireOPD: Self-Retiring On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Yongliang Shen
bullet_points: Introduces RetireOPD, a method for self-retiring on-policy distillation in agentic Reinforcement Learning (RL).
The technique aims to provide dense, token-level supervision to skill-free student agents using a self-teacher.
The research highlights two limitations: teacher reliability is not guaranteed by privileged information, and supervision benefit is stage-dependent.

stories.title: dQwen3.5: Hybrid-Attention Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Sanjay Shakkottai
bullet_points: The research explores adapting existing autoregressive (AR) language models to function as Diffusion Language Models (DLMs).
A key challenge identified is adapting hybrid AR backbones, which interleave attention and RNN layers, due to the structural causality of RNNs.
The paper investigates the feasibility of using these hybrid AR architectures as effective DLMs despite the adaptation difficulties.

stories.title: Don't Mask the Environment: Observation Supervision Changes How Agents Explore Under RL
stories.author: Rashmi Gangadharaiah
bullet_points: The paper challenges the standard practice in RL where only agent actions are supervised during fine-tuning.
It introduces 'ActObs,' a method that extends supervision to include environment observation tokens within agent trajectories.
The research investigates whether supervising observations provides a better initialization point for subsequent Reinforcement Learning.

stories.title: Architecting a Resilient DevSecOps Pipeline for Enterprise AI Agents
stories.author: jitu028
bullet_points: Proposes a four-stage DevSecOps CI/CD architecture specifically for securing enterprise AI agents.
Integrates multiple security tools, including GitHub Actions, secret scanning, Veracode SCA, and Pipeline SAST.
Highlights the use of AI-assisted review within the pipeline for enhanced security practices.
